searchText: Where can I find working bootstrap node enr records for Ethereum mainnet to use with a discv5 client? All ENR records I have found this far don't seem to work. Assuming an example like: `enr:/3.127.134.103:9000?udp=9000` should at least allow a tcp connection on port 9000. https://github.com/ethereum/discv4-dns-lists/tree/master/all.mainnet.ethdisco.net or https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/blob/300df874d789eba38fe652d270c8998c8759937c/params/bootnodes.go#L23 Thanks! This seems to be a good starting point. You can compile devp2p (a tool that you get after running make all in geth's repo), then you can use that to ping: ``` ./devp2p rlpx ping enode://22a8232c3abc76a16ae9d6c3b164f98775fe226f0917b0ca871128a74a8e9630b458460865bab457221f1d448dd9791d24c4e5d88786180ac185df813a68d4de@3.209.45.79:30303 ``` output: ``` {Version:5 Name:Geth/v1.12.2-stable-bed84606/linux-amd64/go1.20.7 Caps:[eth/66 eth/67 eth/68 les/2 les/3 les/4 snap/1] ListenPort:0 ID:[34 168 35 44 58 188 118 161 106 233 214 195 177 100 249 135 117 254 34 111 9 23 176 202 135 17 40 167 74 142 150 48 180 88 70 8 101 186 180 87 34 31 29 68 141 217 121 29 36 196 229 216 135 134 24 10 193 133 223 129 58 104 212 222] Rest:[]} ``` The port number 30303 looks like an execution layer nodes address. I am looking for beacon chain nodes. Yeah they look like EL nodes Does the first link really list discv5 enr records? The url says discv4 😕 https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/blob/300df874d789eba38fe652d270c8998c8759937c/params/bootnodes.go#L67-L83 Getting from the CL client, like lighthouse, is also a good idea https://github.com/sigp/lighthouse/blob/stable/common/eth2_network_config/built_in_network_configs/mainnet/boot_enr.yaml Yeah, I think that's correct, but I'm afraid it may not really be used anywhere because go-ethereum is an EL client. This is what I am looking for! Thanks! Bootnodes by client software Great for debugging 🙂 ah sorry about that, i glossed over and passed you the EL info 😅

excerpts.author: parithosh
excerpts.content:
You can compile devp2p (a tool that you get after running make all in geth's repo), then you can use that to ping:
```
./devp2p rlpx ping enode://22a8232c3abc76a16ae9d6c3b164f98775fe226f0917b0ca871128a74a8e9630b458460865bab457221f1d448dd9791d24c4e5d88786180ac185df813a68d4de@3.209.45.79:30303
```
